<thought>Using the template that converts a fluorinated carbon back to a hydroxyl (reaction_id 1914395), the product SMILES splits into two fragments. The first fragment remains unchanged, while the second fragment’s fluorine is replaced by a hydroxyl, yielding the precursor OC1CN(Cc2ccc(Cn3nnc(Cl)c3Cl)cc2)C1. Therefore the possible precursor combination is the unchanged first fragment together with this new hydroxyl fragment.</thought>
<final_answer>[['COc1cccc(NC=O)c1', 'OC1CN(Cc2ccc(Cn3nnc(Cl)c3Cl)cc2)C1']]</final_answer>
